headline: The documentation and the package's own source comments settle on one spelling of the words they use in both.
summary: The prose mixed British and US spellings of the same words, so a reader searching for one form missed the passages written in the other. Every pair now uses the US form. The changelog is generated, so its share of the corrections is made in the release notes it is built from. No entry changes what it says, and no API, error code or behavior changes.

Changed: Documentation and source comments now use the US spellings behavior, recognize, unrecognized, labeled, honored, license, defense, neighbor, authorize, initialization, signaled, modeled, favor and fulfill. 218 substitutions across 88 files: the README, the security policy, thirteen release notes and the changelog generated from them, the status-lifecycle record, the comments and error text in lib/, and the test suite and release scripts. Two spellings stay as they are: catalogue, the established form here, and Simple Certificate Enrolment Protocol, which is RFC 8894's title and is quoted as published.
